properties.name: dynograph-foundation designates ifc:kv-backend `published` — the seam under StorageEngine — while the code makes `KvBackend` pub(crate), so the one node naming the shared layer beneath the diamond promises an extension point nobody outside can implement
properties.statement:
READ 2026-08-21 in /home/ajs7/project/dynograph-foundation, at Anthony's invitation ("dynograph-foundation is also my project... we can also review it"). READ ONLY — nothing was written to that repo.

ITS DESIGN SAYS: `ifc:kv-backend`, designation **published**, named "KvBackend trait (storage seam)", spec "The narrow seam underneath StorageEngine. All schema-aware behaviour — validation, the reverse index, the read cache, the write-buffer overlay, the full-text sidecar — sits ABOVE this trait; everything that touches bytes goes through it", operations "six byte-level primitives over six named column families, plus ordered prefix iteration".

ITS CODE SAYS: `pub(crate) trait KvBackend: Send + Sync` (crates/dynograph-storage/src/backend.rs:210). Two implementations, `MemoryBackend` and `RocksBackend`. No public re-export found.

⇒ THE SEAM IS REAL AND IT IS NOT REACHABLE. Swappable from INSIDE dynograph-foundation, not from outside it. A new backend — object storage, a networked KV, something sharded — is a change to that repo, not something reflow2 or flo2 could supply. That is fine while one person owns all three and is worth knowing before anyone plans otherwise.

⭐ WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY VISIBILITY MISMATCH. `fact:the-diamond-meets-at-dynographs-internals-not-its-interface` established that reflow2 and storyflow consume DISJOINT surfaces over one shared implementation, and that "neither consumer's graph can see that layer at all". `ifc:kv-backend` is the ONE node in any of these designs that names that layer. So the single place the shared substrate is modelled is also the place where the design and the code disagree about whether anyone may build on it.

⭐ AND IT IS THE SEAM THE 10k QUESTION TURNS ON. `dec:idea-where-does-the-10k-work-actually-land` records the reading that a hosted byte store is a new `impl KvBackend` needing no reflow2 change, because `StorageEngine` holds `Box<dyn KvBackend>` and does not change type. That reading is correct about the SHAPE and depends on this visibility: today only dynograph-foundation can supply one.

📌 ALSO OBSERVED IN THE SAME READ, unprompted and relevant to flo2's architecture: dynograph-foundation already has the hosted-service shape, and it is real in code rather than aspirational. `ifc:rest-v1` is specified 9/9 — 80 operations at /v1, bearer JWT when configured. `ifc:auth-provider` is a PUBLIC trait (`pub use auth::{AuthProvider, BearerJwt, Identity, NoAuth}` in dynograph-service), described as "an EXTENSION POINT", with an integration test asserting a JWT is rejected without a token and accepted with one. There are `dynograph-service` and `dynograph-client` crates, plus `ifc:ops-probes` at 8/9 and a Unix-socket transport. flo2's tracker states "reflow2 has NO AUTHENTICATION and is not getting any — AuthN and authZ are flo2's, at the layer in front", which is true of reflow2 and NOT true of the layer beneath it.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not assumed: whether reflow2 could usefully run as a CLIENT of a dynograph-service rather than embedding StorageEngine. It would not be a `KvBackend` swap — that trait is byte-level and synchronous, and putting HTTP under it per operation would be worse, not better. It would be a swap at the graph-operations level, roughly where `ifc:graph-read` sits. Offered as a shape nobody has costed, not as a recommendation.

⚠️ BOUND: dynograph-foundation's committed export was written by reflow2 0.16.0 on 2026-07-27 and its working tree is at v0.12.0. The design may lag its own code; only the two facts above were checked against source.
